proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 80, 3^n is congruent to 3^(n mod 3) modulo 13.

argument.text: At n = 1 both sides equal 1 modulo 13.
The residue 3 has order 3 modulo 13: for every n in [0, 77], 3^(n+3) is congruent to 3^n modulo 13.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 80 we have n^2 >= 2n.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
For every n in [0, 80]: if 3 divides n then 3^n is congruent to 1 modulo 13.
There exists an integer n in [1, 80] with n^2 > 80.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 80: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 80].
Every n in [0, 80] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 3.
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 80].
